Offline model evaluation · fixed Company A dataset

Why this model was selected

Three separately trained families used the same 681,935 complete examples, 45 past-only features and next-30-minute item-count target. The test period was held back until selection was locked.

Count prediction is a regression task: MAE and RMSE apply; classification accuracy, precision and recall do not. Candidate test scores are displayed for audit, never used for model selection. Test columns are each model fitted on the training block only; the shipped gradient-boosting model was then refit on all pre-test data (test active MAE 2.338). Training time and latency were measured on the training machine.

Selected: Gradient boosting. Its mean validation active MAE was 1.739; the neural network was only 1.45% behind. The last fold favoured boosting by 5.43%. The deployed model was refit on all pre-test data. On the later test period its active MAE was 2.338, versus 3.109 for the simple persistence reference. The winner did not win every fold.
Offline virtual-line control check: with an automatic acceptance policy under identical simulated arrivals and Stage 2 slowdown, control completed 223 items versus 202 without action (+10.4%). Average wait fell from 1805s to 829s (−54.1%). Manual approval in the live demo can change this outcome. These are simulation results, not factory measurements.
Interactive ML lab · fixed Company A data

Train and compare three models

Each button really fits a new model on the same 50,000-row chronological pre-replay demo slice. A 25-minute label embargo protects the validation period. These quick-run scores are separate from the full 681,935-example evaluation above. Train demo model uses the fixed seed, so it repeats exactly; Train with new seed shows how much of a score difference is just randomness. Choosing the luckiest seed would be cherry-picking.
